intro: A weekly reading for the Twin Cities — grounded, kind, and written for where you actually live.

horoscopes.text: You start the day with a clear head and the rest follows. Patience pays out at a rate you would not have predicted. Outside, the kind of warmth you don't notice you needed. Rest comes easily to someone who worked well.
You move through the day like someone who knows where the shortcuts are. You take a longer route home and notice three good things. Open the windows. You will sleep well.
Today, the small talk is genuinely good. You tell a story better than you have ever told it. Somewhere near a back booth at the CC Club. You did enough. Let the day close.
The weather and your mood are in easy agreement. A meal with one other person does most of the good this week. Outside, an east wind off the river. You did beautifully today. Rest in that.
You walk into the room and the room lifts. People say kind things about you when you are not in the room. A glass of water. A long sleep. You earned both.

A small repair, twenty minutes, large and satisfying gain. You solve the thing you have been thinking about and the answer is elegant. Outside, one of those days where the light does most of the work. Fold the laundry, then close the day with satisfaction.
A flower in a window catches you off guard and you stop to look. A small change to the space makes everything feel better. Set the table for tomorrow's breakfast. A small act of care.
A long game you have been playing moves forward today. You finish something that was years in the making. It is good. The work was deep. The sleep will be too.

A book in a free library on a corner you do not usually walk. Take it. A friend you have not talked to in a while reaches out and the conversation is real. Outside, a heavy late-afternoon stillness. A long exhale. The day delivered. Lights out.

You answer the email you had been sitting on. Easier than expected, better too. You are recognized for something real. Receive it fully. Somewhere near the booth nearest the door at Mickey's Diner. A small private celebration of something only you know you accomplished.

A morning that rewards working alone for an hour first. A friend takes your strange idea seriously and it turns out to be a good one. Somewhere near a bench at Loring Park. The next experiment will be there in the morning.

A poem you half-remember comes back with what you needed. A friend shares something real with you. You hold the room perfectly. Outside, the kind of warmth you don't notice you needed. Sleep finds the people who lived the day fully.
